objectClass.notes: Eight public part types: four blade layers and four hilt part types. The identity rests on exactly four slim drivers in mirrored pairs, a sharpened pale shell over an unsharpened violet insert, and the absence of any surface microdetail.

reasoning: Two macro assemblies (blade, hilt) resolving into eight independently reviewable public part types.
One repetition system: four drivers, two per side, sharing one geometry and four transforms.

Nine distinct material zones. The shell was the main technical risk while it was translucent - ordering an alpha-blended hull over opaque inserts - and it is SOLID since 2026-08-07 by user direction, which retires that risk and replaces it with an occlusion one: a layer that does not physically break the shell is now deleted rather than washed out.
Occlusion risk is high: the blade root and all four driver roots are hidden behind the guard, and the dark core's lower half shares the crop's dark run with the gem it surrounds.
Zero microtexture — the flat faceted language is itself identity-defining, so adding relief is a failure mode, not an improvement.

details.description: The pale shell carries a longitudinal centre ridge; thickness falls from the ridge to zero at both side edges
Both lateral margins thin into bevelled cutting edges — the shell is the only sharpened blade layer
Width knee: half-width peaks at 82 at Y=70, then falls near-linearly at -0.059/unit
Below the insert's base line (Y=42, half-width 72) the shell converges to the clamps' own outer lower vertex at (+/-34, 13) and stops there; no pale geometry exists below the jaws
Background is visible between the shell silhouette and every driver: 25.1 units in front view = 1.14 driver diameters, against a floor of 0.75
Second knee at Y=575 (half-width 54) where the taper breaks to -0.29/unit into the point
Three flat lavender value bands (#E6E7F2 / #CDCFD8 / #B5B6BF) with no smooth ramp between them
Above Y=380 the insert's sides break to -0.28/unit, forming the small triangular point at Y=480
The insert's side faces stay square and faceted — it never receives the shell's knife-edge bevel
First skin: a film 0.05 T thick laid on the shell's own front and rear surfaces, following that surface in X and in Y, never touching Z=0
Vertical ramp runs dark at the apex (#160D59) to bright at the base (#7F3CF2) — inverted from surface shading, so it reads as emitted energy
Narrow centred upward triangle over the insert's lower half; never widens into a central panel
Second skin: the same film 0.05 T thick, seated on the insert's outer face rather than on the shell, so the two stack and the order cannot invert
Elongated rhombus, 84 tall by 34 wide (2.5:1), waist at Y=55 level with the clamp jaws' contact line
The one raised BODY on the blade: a girdled rhombus seated on the two skins, its rim standing 0.12 T outside them at every station and its crown a further 0.38 of its own half-width above that rim
The gem's front splits into a lighter and a darker facet along its vertical axis
The guard closes with no bridge part in it: the two jaws carry a flat floor at Y=13 and the grip column's flat top lies against it, face to face
Both leather connector arms rake outward-downward from the jaws' outer corners, at the shell's own lower taper turned into an angle

Each arm ends in a faceted frustum hanging vertically, WIDEST AT THE TOP and narrowing all the way down: a derived seat ring buried inside the leather, a shoulder 1.5 below it at radius 24.3, then one straight line to a blunt truncation at 8.1 rather than a point
One thin bright edge strip (#BB2A50) runs the length of each wine-red rod
All four driver axes converge at (0, -62) — below the guard centre, not at it
Each rod's root cap is buried inside its connector arm, deep enough that the whole cap rim clears the leather and never as deep as the arm's own axis — there is no socket mesh
Two mirrored triangular jaws cradle the diamond's lower half and meet on the axis at the culet, sharing that one vertical edge and no face
The shaft holds half-width 12 from the jaws' floor at Y=13 to its measured lower edge at -180 — no waist, no T
No collar anywhere on the shaft: at 16x the leather runs uniform to -180 and the gold starts on the next row

The pointed pommel is one straight cone from the leather's own lower edge to the tip at -210.7. Its base ring is the column's bottom ring — same circumradius 12, same 8 facets — so its front-view reach is the column's own 11.087 and the junction cannot open

Tip, guard centre, gem centre, grip end, and all four driver endpoints within 2.5% of image height.

The shell reads as sharpened and the insert as blunt from the form-refinement pass onward.

coordinateFrame.scaleReference: normalized-1000 divided by 100; the object stands 9.707 world units tall
coordinateFrame.componentTransform: Every componentTree entry's transform.position is its BUILT bounding-box centre, read from artifacts/ultima-v2/full/parts.json, and dimensions are that box's own extents. They are not authored numbers and must not be edited by hand.
coordinateFrame.socketConvention: actionProfile.sockets[].localPosition is relative to that component's own transform.position, so a socket's world point is position + localPosition. Both ends of every attachment declare the joint's anchor, and spec/audit_records.py asserts that the parentSocket and the childSocket resolve to the SAME world point. Anchors that describe an OUTLINE coincidence lie in the outline plane Z = 0; anchors that describe a SEAT carry the depth of the surface they sit on.

Flat normals throughout; every quad carries its own normal so no facet is smoothed away by shared vertices. The rods are faceted cylinders at eight segments, which is a cylinder in the PS1 sense, not a smooth one.
No sort inversion observed across the orbit; the multi-angle gate reports no degenerate view.
Unchanged by the lighting rig; the transmissive pass ordering is a renderer concern, not a light one.
The rig is near-ambient on purpose. Shading is already baked into vertex colour, so a strong key would shade an already-shaded surface and crush the near-white shell.

Every node in the correction spec's ownership tree is selectable and explodable: crystalClampLeft/Right, both leather connectors, both spinner ends, the driverArray with its four rods, the grip and the pommel. There is no guardCore, no driver socket and no grip end collar to expose — those were components of earlier passes and all of them are deleted rather than hidden.

The grip and the pommel are separate selectable nodes and the explode pulls them apart in that order. There is no collar between them; the grip's own tang carries the guard end of the stack, so the two jaws explode off the leather they were closed on.
Unchanged by the interaction wiring.
No merging: every part stays its own mesh so the inspector and the explode keep working.
580 triangles at full detail. No decimation applied — every authored plane is load-bearing for the PS1 facet reading, and the budget is two orders of magnitude under the real-time target anyway.

Blockout carries the outer shell only; the three inset layers change no outline and arrive with the structural pass. The shell's own profile matches the measured artwork within 3-5% at every band, and its lower section now converges symmetrically into the guard instead of stopping as a slab.
Four rods present, two per side, mirrored. Endpoints land on the measured (+/-126, 54) and (+/-155, 12); all four axes converge at (0, -62) as measured.
Blade 760, grip 163 of constant width, collar 14, pommel 31 in normalized-1000. Tip and pommel-tip errors stay inside 1% of image height against a 2.5% budget.
All four blade parts present and correctly ordered front to back: gem, dark core, violet insert, pale shell. The shell clears the insert by at least 54 units per side at every height.
Exactly four instances of one shared geometry placed by four transforms. Verified in the exploded view: no rod is independently remodelled.

Each rod is a faceted cylinder of radius 11 with eight radial segments, and each enters its own socket collar (radii 52-68 on the same axis). The socket is deliberately shorter than the rod's root taper so the taper straddles the mouth and the insertion reads in the close-up. The rods sit at Z=0 with a real circular section, not pushed forward onto the guard's front face.

Two mirrored jaws, inner edges running (17,48)->(11,16) so each stays outside the gem's half-width at every station, lower ends landing on the central socket's shoulders at (24,3). The pair stops short of meeting at the centre, which is what keeps it from reading as one chevron.
Unchanged from the blockout; the structural pass adds no length-bearing geometry.
Central socket plus two leather arms raked -50 degrees, each ending in a compact spinner. Narrow and subordinate to the blade and the four rods.

The shell's eight-point section falls to zero thickness at both side edges and peaks at a centre ridge. Below the measured base it contracts through two mirrored slopes (80 -> 52 -> 26 -> 18 half-width) into a neck seated inside the central socket. The insert's six-point section keeps square sides and takes no bevel.

Root taper and capped outer end both cut. The shell's new neck is narrow enough that the rods clear it on their own: the upper rod's innermost point is at |X|=40 where the neck is 26 wide, so no rod passes through the crystal.
Jaws faceted to four planes, half-depth 9, straddling the gem in Z at +17 against the gem's +19. They cradle without intersecting.
Connector arms are six-sided wrapped limbs rather than boxes, half-width 15-17. Each spinner end runs radius 5 at the neck, 18 at the bulge, then a point over 50 units.

Four-sided bipyramid, 84 tall by 34 wide, front vertex 11 proud of the waist. Its Z stack was pulled in from +30 to +19 because at the old depth the front vertex reached Z=45 against a 13-deep blade and read as bolted onto the front.

Grip holds half-width 12 from the guard connection to the collar. All three protruding ring meshes are gone; the wrap is vertex-colour banding on the same shaft. One collar at Y=-166..-180, then an independent pommel with maximum radius 11.

All nine measured zones stay separable in the render. The residual is a global value offset, not a hue error: the shell renders about two thirds of a stop below the reference's #E6E7F2, which is what drives the tier-1 per-part delta-E failure.
Transmission 0.30 with flat facets keeps the gem reading as a crystal rather than a painted shape.
Facet value steps are baked into vertex colour in three flat bands, so they stay hard-edged at any lighting setting. No normal or displacement map anywhere.
Shell and gem both use transmission and therefore three's transmissive pass, which sorts after opaque; the inset layers are additionally spaced in Z so no ordering is left to the sorter alone.

reviewHistory.summary: Macro silhouette holds through both correction passes. Registered silhouette IoU 0.8561; tip 1.00%, pommel 0.59%, lateral extremes 1.00%/1.00% of image height against a 2.5% budget. The tier-1 blockout gate is RED at 0.8175 against a 0.85 floor, and every step down is a user direction rather than a defect: 0.8553 to 0.8478 on 2026-08-11 when both arms came up onto the jaws' outer corners, to 0.8367 on 2026-08-12 when the arms were directed longer so the spinner balls hang lower, to 0.8348 on 2026-08-13 when the caps became frusta widest at the top, and to 0.8175 later that day when the arms were directed longer again and the caps shortened with them. Swept over the arm's length and over CONNECTOR_RADIUS, nothing but reverting the directions recovers it - a documented limitation, CURRENT-MODEL.md section 8. The floor and the IoU computation are untouched.
matched: blade tip at Y=760 and pommel tip at Y=-211 both within 1% of image height
the shell converges from its widest half-width 82 at Y=70 into the two clamp contact points at (+/-31.57, 13), above the jaws' own lowest vertex
four drivers reach the measured endpoints (+/-125, 56) and (+/-155, 12)
mismatches: the shell's own maximum half-width dropped from 95 to 88 when the base flare was re-read as a projection artifact
that is a deliberate change, not drift
